subject: Reasoning
description: Angles between clock hands, mirror time, clock arithmetic

questions.stem: Angle between hour + minute hand at 3:00:
questions.explanation: At 3:00, hour hand is on 3, minute on 12. They are 3 hour-divisions apart. Each hour-division = 30° (full circle 360°/12 = 30°). So angle = 3 × 30° = 90°. KEY FORMULAS: (1) Angle of hour hand from 12 = (H × 30) + (M × 0.5) (since hour hand moves 0.5° per minute too). (2) Angle of minute hand from 12 = M × 6 (full revolution = 60 min, so 360/60 = 6° per minute). (3) Angle BETWEEN hands = |30H − 5.5M| (smaller of this and 360−this). At 3:00: |30×3 − 5.5×0| = 90°. INSIGHT — TWO ANGLES are formed (always sum to 360°); usually 'angle between' = smaller one (acute or obtuse).

questions.stem: How many times do hour + minute hands COINCIDE in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Hour + minute hands COINCIDE 11 times in 12 hours (NOT 12). Why: minute hand laps hour hand once per ~65.45 min (= 720/11 min). In 12 hours = 720 min → 720/65.45 ≈ 11 times. Common confusion: hands coincide once per hour, BUT not exactly at the start of each hour after 12. Between 11 + 1, hands meet only ONCE (not twice) — that's at 12:00. Hence 11. SIMILAR: hands form right angle (90°) 22 times in 12 hours; STRAIGHT LINE (180°) 11 times. INSIGHT — 24 hours: 22 coincidences, 44 right angles, 22 straight-lines. Pattern: per 12 hr, each is 11 × multiplier (1×, 2×, 1×).

questions.stem: Angle between hour + minute hand at 4:30:
questions.explanation: Use formula |30H − 5.5M|: |30×4 − 5.5×30| = |120 − 165| = 45°. So 45°. INTERPRETATION: At 4:30, minute hand on 6 (180° from 12). Hour hand at 4 + half-way to 5 = 4.5 × 30 = 135° from 12. Difference = 180 − 135 = 45°. SAME formula works for any time. EXAMPLES: at 6:00 → |180 − 0| = 180° (straight). At 3:30 → |90 − 165| = 75°. At 12:00 → |0 − 0| = 0° (coincide). PRACTICE this one formula — covers all clock-angle questions.

questions.stem: Mirror image of clock showing 6:30 will show:
questions.explanation: MIRROR IMAGE OF CLOCK rule: subtract given time from 11:60 (i.e., 12:00 minus given). 11:60 − 6:30 = 5:30. ALWAYS use this trick: original + mirror = 11:60. EXCEPTIONS: if original > 11:00 OR is 11:60 (= 12:00), special handling. EXAMPLES: 8:30 → mirror = 11:60 − 8:30 = 3:30. 9:15 → 11:60 − 9:15 = 2:45. 12:00 → 11:60 (use 23:60 if past noon...). INSIGHT — vertical mirror (like wall mirror) flips left-right. So 12 stays at 12, 6 stays at 6, but other numbers swap (1↔11, 2↔10, 3↔9, 4↔8, 5↔7). Hour hand position swaps similarly. Common in IBPS PO + SSC clock problems.

questions.stem: MINUTE hand of a clock moves how many degrees per MINUTE?
questions.explanation: MINUTE hand: 360° in 60 min → 6° per minute. HOUR hand: 360° in 720 min (12 hrs × 60) → 0.5° per minute (= 30° per hour, the dial division). RELATIVE speed: minute - hour = 5.5° per minute (this is why minute laps hour every 720/11 min). KEY DIFFERENCE: at 12:00 both hands point to 12; minute hand catches up with hour at 1:05+ (not exactly 1:05 — slight after, because hour also moves). USE 5.5°/min as relative speed in clock problems.

questions.stem: A clock loses 5 min in 24 hours. How much will it lose in 1 week?
questions.explanation: Loss/day = 5 min → loss/week (7 days) = 5 × 7 = 35 min. SIMPLE PROPORTION. Same logic for time-gain clocks (running fast). PRACTICAL: this is what 'rate of error' means in old mechanical clocks (modern quartz watches lose ~15 sec/month, atomic clocks lose 1 sec in millions of years!). IMPLICATIONS: when clock loses 5 min/day, after 144 days it loses 12 hours = appears to show correct time again (one cycle). FORMULA: time to coincide again = 12 hr / (loss or gain rate per hour). 5 min/day = 5/24 min/hr → 12×60/(5/24) = 17,280/(5/24) = 3456 hrs = 144 days.

questions.stem: At what time between 4 + 5 o'clock will the hands form a STRAIGHT LINE (i.e., 180°)?
questions.explanation: Want |30H − 5.5M| = 180° between 4 + 5. With H = 4: |120 − 5.5M| = 180 → 5.5M = 120 ± 180 → 5.5M = 300 or −60. Take positive: 5.5M = 300 → M = 300/5.5 = 600/11 ≈ 54.55. So time ≈ 4:54 6/11 min. INSIGHT — every hour, hands form 180° EXACTLY ONCE (with some rare exceptions near 6:00, where it happens AT 6:00 itself). Hands form 90° (right angle) twice per hour (mostly). Form 0° (coincide) once per hour (mostly). Use the formula |30H − 5.5M| = required angle, solve for M.
